response.query: Which numeric HU-fidelity thresholds (mean absolute HU error and SD) will we require in defined ROIs (vessel lumen, lung parenchyma, mediastinal soft tissue) to pass pilot QA?
response.answer: For pilot QA, vessel lumen: <5 HU MAE, lung parenchyma: <35 HU MAE, mediastinal soft tissue: <10 HU MAE.

results.title: Emphysema Quantifications With CT Scan: Assessing the Effects of Acquisition Protocols and Imaging Parameters Using Virtual Imaging Trials - PMC
results.content: The most accurate imaging condition corresponded to the highest acquired dose (100 mAs) and iterative reconstruction (SAFIRE) with the smooth kernel of I31, where the measurement errors (difference between measurement and ground truth) were 35 ± 3 Hounsfield Units (HU), −4% ± 5%, and 26 ± 10 HU (average ± SD), for the mean lung HU, LAA-950, and Perc15, respectively. For the healthy organs and structures, both density and elemental compositions were set based on the International Commission for Radiation Units report 46.18 For the emphysema regions, the elemental compositions were defined as lung parenchyma, and the density was set based on measurements from the COPDGene CT scan cases to provide diverse density values across the library of modeled patients. The reconstructed CT scan images were compared against the corresponding reference ground truth phantoms in terms of mean absolute error (MAE), and lung histogram-based imaging biomarkers. The histograms of the lung parenchyma regions were measured in the CT scan images and compared against the ground truth values in terms of three histogram features: mean histogram, LAA-950 (percent of lung voxels with HU < −950), Perc15 (15th percentile of lung histogram HU). These LAA-950 and Perc15 were chosen because prior studies have shown their predictive capabilities in COPD assessments.6 For each CT scan dataset and imaging biomarker, the accuracy of the histogram features were derived by subtracting the measured biomarker with the reference, ground truth value in the corresponding phantom. Furthermore, to compare against previous studies on physical phantoms,23, 24, 25 median HU was measured in the lung parenchyma of the reconstructed CT images across all the acquired imaging conditions. Figure 7 shows the quantitative evaluation of the lung MAE, emphysema MAE, the accuracy of mean lung HU, LAA-950, and Perc15, and the measured median lung HU values across all the studied imaging parameters. This study comprehensively explored the effects of imaging parameters (dose level, tube current modulation, and reconstruction algorithm and kernel) on CT scan quantifications for COPD imaging using the novel approach of virtual imaging trials. The emphysema models in this study included diverse sizes, shapes, patterns, and densities, informed by CT scan images.

results.title: In-vivo lung fibrosis staging in a bleomycin-mouse model: a new micro-CT guided densitometric approach | Scientific Reports
results.content: To the best of our knowledge, the HU ranges used to define differently aerated lung compartments vary from investigator to investigator, depending on the animal species or on the disease (Table1)17."),19."),21."),23."),24."),25.")**.** Nevertheless, standardized density thresholds for characterizing lung disorders could be of critical importance when comparing different animal models or testing different treatments in drug discovery processes18."). A semi-automatic segmentation is used to define the whole lung volume when the parenchyma is detectable and well defined by the threshold range (e.g. vehicles or mild and moderate lesions in pathological subjects) Fig. 1a, b**.** This approach was considered acceptable for the BLM-induced murine fibrosis model analyzed herein and it was used to define aeration levels in mice as detailed below. A manual segmentation is necessary to correctly identify lung regions that are not clearly detectable due to lack of aeration, absence of clear boundaries and jagged or severely damaged parenchyma (i.e. areas of massive fibrosis in pathological subjects)35.") (Fig. 1c)**.** The manual approach was required for only 2–3% of the mice that underwent the OA administration procedures described previously. To characterize global changes in the lung during fibrosis progression and to evaluate the therapeutic effects of the compounds under investigation, we used the segmentation map to extract several micro-CT quantitative parameters: lung volume [mm3], mean lung density [HU], standard deviation of the mean, maximum and minimum HU values within the region-of-interest (ROI). As a step forward, we used the value – 435 HU (red dotted lines in Fig. 4b, d), namely the mean between the lowest 70th percentile in BLM groups and the highest 70th percentile in saline groups (n = 100), to define lung aeration regions in mice. Following the same procedure, the hypo-aerated region was defined by fixing its upper limit at – 121 HU, namely the highest HU value reached in lung density histograms using automatic segmentation (n = 100). In this work, we evaluated the use of micro-CT density measurements in a murine model of BLM-induced lung fibrosis, defining reference values for the quantification of longitudinal changes in lung parenchyma. *et al.* Longitudinal assessment of bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis by micro-CT correlates with histological evaluation in mice.

Title: CT - Radiology Cafe
# CT. CT (computed tomography) uses X-rays to obtain images. X-rays pass through tissues and hit a detector on the other side. The more dense a tissue, the more X-rays it absorbs. In a CT chest/abdo/pelvis, the lung bases/liver may be imaged twice (overlap between chest – arterial phase, and abdomen – venous phase). Tissue density is measured in Hounsfield units (HU). Density of tissues on CT:. Air < Fat < Fluid < Soft tissue < Bone < Metal. * Lung ≈ −500 HU (partially air, partially soft tissue). * Soft tissue (& blood) ≈ +50 HU (slightly more dense than simple fluid). For example, a window with a level of 0 HU and a width of 400 HU will have a range of −200 HU to +200 HU. Any tissue with a density of −200 HU or less will be black, and any tissue with a density of +200 HU or more will be white. Examples of commonly used windows are soft tissue, lung, and bone. #### Soft tissue window. A soft tissue window is used to view most organs. A soft tissue window cannot be used for lung parenchyma, as lung density (−500 HU) is outside range and will appear completely black. Soft tissue window on a chest CT. Soft tissue window on a chest CT. Lung parenchyma (−500 HU) would be within range, appearing grey. Lung window on a chest CT. Lung window on a chest CT. Bone tissue window on a chest CT. Bone tissue window on a chest CT. | **Chest X-ray** | 0.02 mSv | 3 days |. | **Abdo X-ray** | 0.7 mSv | 3 months |. | **Head CT** | 2 mSv | 9 months |. | **Chest CT** | 7 mSv | 2.5 years |. | **Abdo CT** | 8 mSv | 3 years |. * Poor renal function (eGFR <30) – non-contrast CT or alternative modalities used. No absolute contraindications to CT, main concern is over contrast and radiation dose. Other uses of CT include high-resolution CT (HRCT) protocol for imaging interstitial lung disease, virtual 3D CT colonogram as an alternative to invasive colonoscopy, and CT-guided biopsies.
